newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat demands Netanyahu curb Sharon on settlement.
newsitem.headline: Arafat demands Netanyahu curb Sharon on settlement.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has demanded Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu clearly state his settlement policy and curb his minister Ariel Sharon who has said settlement of occupied lands will increase.
"Arafat sent a letter to Netanyahu asking him to clearly state his settlement policy and to stop statements like those of Sharon," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said on Thursday.
Erekat told Reuters that during talks on Wednesday he passed the letter to his Israeli counterpart to deliver to Netanyahu.
Infrastructure Minister Sharon has recently said planning is going on for the establishment of a new Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank.

The Israeli Housing Ministry confirmed it was planning such a new settlement near the West Bank Palestinian enclave of Ramallah but that it had many approval stages to pass and the government had yet to give its blessing to the project.

The right-wing Netanyahu, shortly after coming to power in June, lifted a settlement building freeze imposed by the centre-left government he ousted, but so far only expansion of existing settlements has been approved under his government.
A senior aide to Netanyahu, asked this week about plans for a new settlement, said the government had not ruled out building new settlements but neither had it decided to do so.

"It has not decided either for or against new settlements but it has established the right of Jews to live in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu's communications director David Bar-Illan told Reuters, using biblical names for the West Bank.
The government must approve the building of a new settlement in the occupied lands. Approval of expansion of existing settlements rests with Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
"The decision of the two ministers is not a government decision. It is an announcement of intent. It is not even a government proposal yet," Bar-Illan said.
Some 130,000 Jews have settled amongst the nearly two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.
Palestinians view the settlers as a provocation and vehemently oppose any expansion of Jewish settlement in territories where they hope to build an independent state.
After meeting Netanyahu on Thursday, Jewish settler leaders who complain that he has moved too slowly on settlement, said they had suspended protests they had planned.

"We very much hope we will not have to demonstrate against the Netanyahu government...For the meantime, we've suspended protest activities...that were organised for today until next week," settler spokesman Aharon Domb told Israel Radio.
